answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a refundable stake plus a history of peer-verified work, not to raw account count. A newcomer starts like a single juniper seedling in a wide oasis: it may transact, but its votes and rewards stay small until established peers attest its real jobs over time. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs stake and effort each time, while a comet-like burst of new accounts with no work history earns nothing. Sybils become expensive to plant and cheap to ignore.
